title: Scenario pool's session shape runs six pool questions in one claude -p session and records the marginal input and cache-read share of each follow-up
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run pool --shape session runs groups of six pool rows (mixed kinds, a seed) in one claude -p session per group on the kb arms haiku-5-5 and sonnet-5-5, each follow-up sent with --resume (or the --session-id of the first run), and records per question its position in the session, marginal_input (the request's input beyond the one before it), cache_read_share (cache reads over input) and checks, beside the per-session rows of shape fresh; bench_report.py prints a marginal-input table by position and arm in the pool section; a test feeds a synthetic six-request transcript and checks the marginal and share values; kb/_self/tools.md names the shape

gates.question: How does a follow-up question of a session group reach the first question's session?
Which seed orders the pool rows into groups of six?
options: the pool's SEED, overridable with --seed on run
a fresh random seed each run
gates.recommendation: the pool's SEED, overridable with --seed on run
gates.answer: the pool's SEED, overridable with --seed on run

gates.question: Which arms and effort levels does the session shape run by default?
options: haiku-5-5 and sonnet-5-5, each at low and default
haiku-5-5 and sonnet-5-5 at default only
gates.recommendation: haiku-5-5 and sonnet-5-5, each at low and default
gates.answer: haiku-5-5 and sonnet-5-5, each at low and default

notes: The shape closest to real use: an operator asks several lookups in one session, so the fixed context is paid once and cache reads carry the rest; today every paid scenario starts a fresh session per question, so marginal cost per follow-up is unmeasured. Mechanism: kb-lookup-agent and always-on already keep a session (--session-id, --no-session-persistence off) and read the transcript per request (bench_core); a follow-up is claude -p --resume SID or -c in the same cwd. Six questions per group, mixed kinds, no two variants of one fact in a group. kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md Isolation already states the throwaway clone; the session's transcript stays under the scratch directory.
